# emss

## Overview

This package aims to support Embedded Standard Setting, calculating counts and weights.


## Install


```{r}
devtools::install_github("sooyongl/emss", dependencies = T)
```

## Usage

```{r eval = T}
library(emss)
```

```{r eval = T}
fake_data <- genFakeDataSet(ngca = 3, 
               cor_val = 0.2,
               n = 30,
               nlevel = 3,
               ntable = 5,
               npanelist = 5,
               sdinp = 1,
               ecinp = 0,
               100,300)



fake_data

# Or you can use your own data structured by the following table.
```

```{r eval = T}
res <- emstans(data = fake_data,
               grades = c(1, 2),
               location = "Loc_RP50",
               method = "weight",
               smooth = FALSE)

```


## Your own data

An emss Excel workbook (sheets Setup, Panelists, Ratings, ItemMetaData,
ExamineeMetaData) can be passed directly:

```{r}
res <- emstans("my_study.xlsx", location = "RP67")
```

Data in other layouts, such as CSV files, go through `ess_data()`. Only
ratings and items are required. Level labels, SD and EC can come from a
setup table, from arguments, or both (arguments win). Columns whose names
differ from the defaults are mapped by name or by position:

```{r}
d <- ess_data(
  ratings = "ratings.csv",
  items   = "items.csv",
  levels  = c("Basic", "Intermediate", "Advanced"),  # lowest to highest
  ec      = 0.3,
  columns = list(ratings = list(panelist = "Rater", level = 8))
)
d                      # overview of what was read
res <- emstans(data = d, location = "RP50")
```

Level labels may also differ by grade:
`levels = list(R1 = c("E", "M", "L"), R2 = c("B", "P", "A"))`. Every table,
plot and report shows the labels, in level order.

When the ratings include several rounds, each grade and round is analysed
separately, and results are named by unit, for example `R1-All Round 2`.

## Plots

```{r eval = T, fig.height = 4}
plot(res, "profile", "M1-All")   # inconsistency profile of the modal result
```

## Summary

```{r eval = T}
summary(res)
```


## Report

With `what = "all"`, the combined report is provided.

### Individual 

```{r eval = T}
report(res, what = "individual")
```

### Detailed 

```{r eval = T}
report(res, what = "detailed")
```


### Summary

```{r eval = T}
report(res, what = "summary")
```

### Item Review 

```{r eval = T}
report(res, what = "review")
```


## Extract

`extract()` provides the primary results of ESS as a form of `list()`.

```{r eval = T}
extract(res)
```
